options.C: Cover up the manipulation so regulators never find out
options.D: Train all other traders to copy the same manipulation

correctAnswer: Dismiss the trader, return ill-gotten gains, self-report the breach to financial regulators, and tighten internal controls

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because ethical integrity requires rejecting profits earned through dishonesty, holding wrongdoers accountable, and cooperating with regulators.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because ethical integrity requires rejecting profits earned through dishonesty, holding wrongdoers accountable, and cooperating with regulators.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because rewarding misconduct destroys ethical culture and invites massive regulatory penalties.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because covering up financial crime compounds legal liability.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because institutionalising market manipulation would destroy the bank.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A social media platform introduces default screen-time reminders and disables addictive infinite-scroll features for users under 18, even though this slightly reduces daily ad impressions. What does this decision demonstrate?

options.A: Prioritising teenage mental wellbeing and digital ethics over maximum short-term advertising revenue
options.B: Attempting to increase teen addiction to mobile screens
options.C: Violating data protection laws
options.D: Eliminating all users over the age of 18

correctAnswer: Prioritising teenage mental wellbeing and digital ethics over maximum short-term advertising revenue

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because voluntarily curbing addictive design features for minors puts user welfare above short-term ad clicks.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because voluntarily curbing addictive design features for minors puts user welfare above short-term ad clicks.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because disabling infinite scroll and adding reminders *reduces* addictive usage.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because protecting young users enhances responsible governance.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adult users remain on the platform.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why might a business operating in a highly price-competitive, low-margin commodity industry (such as basic bulk gravel or unbranded sugar) find it harder to pass on higher ethical sourcing costs to customers than a branded coffee shop?

options.A: Commodity buyers view the product as identical and switch immediately to the cheapest rival, whereas branded coffee drinkers are willing to pay a premium for ethical values
options.B: Commodity businesses are legally forbidden from behaving ethically
options.C: Branded coffee shops never pay for raw coffee beans
options.D: Gravel quarries do not have any employees or suppliers

correctAnswer: Commodity buyers view the product as identical and switch immediately to the cheapest rival, whereas branded coffee drinkers are willing to pay a premium for ethical values

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because brand differentiation allows consumer-facing firms to monetise ethical values via price premiums, whereas undifferentiated commodities compete purely on price.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because brand differentiation allows consumer-facing firms to monetise ethical values via price premiums, whereas undifferentiated commodities compete purely on price.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because all businesses can behave ethically, though cost recovery differs by market structure.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because coffee shops purchase roasted coffee beans at significant cost.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because quarries employ workers and use equipment suppliers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A clothing company publishes a list of every single factory it uses worldwide, including factory addresses, worker numbers, and recent independent audit scores, on its public website. How does this 'supply-chain transparency' benefit the company?

options.A: It demonstrates accountability, builds trust with consumers and human rights NGOs, and deters factory abuses
options.B: It allows the company to hide sweatshop conditions from the public
options.C: It lowers import tariffs to zero automatically
options.D: It stops competitors from ever making clothes

correctAnswer: It demonstrates accountability, builds trust with consumers and human rights NGOs, and deters factory abuses

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because radical transparency proves the brand has nothing to hide and invites constructive accountability across its supply network.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because radical transparency proves the brand has nothing to hide and invites constructive accountability across its supply network.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because publishing factory locations makes conditions *visible*, not hidden.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because tariff rates are set by customs laws, not website disclosures.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because competitors still operate normally.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: When a supermarket chain donates 1% of its pre-tax profits every year to local youth sports clubs and community food pantries, which term best describes this activity?

options.A: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and community philanthropy
options.B: Hostile horizontal takeover
options.C: Price discrimination
options.D: Tax evasion

correctAnswer: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and community philanthropy

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because voluntary financial and social contributions to improve local community wellbeing are a core pillar of CSR.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because voluntary financial and social contributions to improve local community wellbeing are a core pillar of CSR.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because a takeover involves acquiring a rival company.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because price discrimination involves charging different customer groups different prices.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because charitable donations are legitimate CSR, not illegal tax evasion.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A recruitment agency removes candidates' names, photos, addresses, and university names from job applications before sending them to hiring managers ('blind recruitment'). What ethical goal does this achieve?

options.A: Preventing unconscious bias based on gender, ethnicity, age, or social background so hiring is based strictly on skills and merit
options.B: Ensuring only candidates from wealthy neighbourhoods are hired
options.C: Making it impossible to contact successful candidates for interviews
options.D: Lowering the statutory minimum wage for new hires

correctAnswer: Preventing unconscious bias based on gender, ethnicity, age, or social background so hiring is based strictly on skills and merit

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because anonymising personal identifiers promotes genuine equal opportunity and fair merit-based selection.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because anonymising personal identifiers promotes genuine equal opportunity and fair merit-based selection.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because removing addresses eliminates postcode/wealth bias.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because HR retains contact details separately to invite shortlisted candidates.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because blind recruitment ensures fair selection, not lower wages.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A fast-food restaurant advertises a 'Giant Double Steak Burger' using professional food styling where the burger looks twice as large as the actual sandwich served to customers. Why is this an ethical and legal issue?

options.A: Misleading advertising deceives consumers, breaches advertising standards codes, and damages customer trust
options.B: Customers always enjoy receiving smaller portions than advertised
options.C: Food photography is illegal in all restaurants
options.D: Smaller burgers increase customer satisfaction scores

correctAnswer: Misleading advertising deceives consumers, breaches advertising standards codes, and damages customer trust

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because deceptive product representation violates ethical marketing principles and consumer protection rules.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because deceptive product representation violates ethical marketing principles and consumer protection rules.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because feeling misled frustrates customers and reduces repeat visits.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because accurate food photography is completely legal.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because unmet expectations lower customer satisfaction.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A company's Board of Directors links 25% of senior executives' annual bonuses to achieving verified targets for workplace safety, staff retention, and carbon reduction alongside financial profit. Why is this governance structure effective?

options.A: It aligns managers' personal financial incentives with long-term ethical and sustainable performance rather than short-term profit alone
options.B: It guarantees that the company will never make any profit
options.C: It encourages managers to ignore workplace safety
options.D: It eliminates the need for employees to follow safety rules

correctAnswer: It aligns managers' personal financial incentives with long-term ethical and sustainable performance rather than short-term profit alone

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because tying executive pay to non-financial ethical metrics ensures leaders treat ethics as a core strategic priority.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because tying executive pay to non-financial ethical metrics ensures leaders treat ethics as a core strategic priority.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because 75% of the bonus remains tied to financial performance and sustainable firms remain profitable.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because linking bonuses to safety motivates managers to *improve* safety.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because all workers and managers must follow safety procedures.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A global coffee chain closes all 8,000 of its stores for one afternoon—losing millions of dollars in daily sales—to conduct mandatory anti-bias and inclusive customer service training for all 175,000 employees after an incident in one store. Why did management make this costly decision?

options.A: To demonstrate genuine commitment to ethical values, repair brand reputation, and prevent future discrimination across the chain
options.B: Because the company wanted to permanently go out of business
options.C: Because coffee beans had become illegal to sell
options.D: To avoid paying employees their afternoon wages

correctAnswer: To demonstrate genuine commitment to ethical values, repair brand reputation, and prevent future discrimination across the chain

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because decisive, visible investment in staff values protects long-term brand equity even at high short-term revenue cost.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because decisive, visible investment in staff values protects long-term brand equity even at high short-term revenue cost.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because the closure was for a single afternoon to strengthen the brand's future.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because coffee sales resumed immediately after training.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because staff were paid to attend the mandatory training session.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: How can unethical business practices in a single company eventually lead to stricter government laws affecting the entire industry?

options.A: Public scandals and media outrage force governments to pass new regulations that impose higher compliance costs on all firms in the sector
options.B: Governments reward unethical scandals by removing all industry regulations
options.C: Unethical scandals automatically reduce compliance costs for competitors
options.D: Lawmakers ignore all major corporate scandals

correctAnswer: Public scandals and media outrage force governments to pass new regulations that impose higher compliance costs on all firms in the sector

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because when businesses fail to self-regulate ethically, governments step in with statutory laws to protect stakeholders.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because when businesses fail to self-regulate ethically, governments step in with statutory laws to protect stakeholders.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because scandals prompt *tighter*, not looser, regulation.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because new statutory rules raise compliance costs across the industry.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because public outcry pressures politicians to legislate.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is the primary difference between a pressure group and a political party?

options.A: A pressure group seeks to influence specific business practices or government policies on particular issues without seeking to form the government itself
options.B: A pressure group runs candidates to become prime minister and run the whole country
options.C: A pressure group is a profit-making public limited company
options.D: A pressure group has the legal authority to pass criminal laws

correctAnswer: A pressure group seeks to influence specific business practices or government policies on particular issues without seeking to form the government itself

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because pressure groups focus on advocating specific causes (environmental, consumer, ethical) rather than winning general elections to govern.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because pressure groups focus on advocating specific causes (environmental, consumer, ethical) rather than winning general elections to govern.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because contesting elections to form a government is the role of a political party.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because pressure groups are non-profit advocacy organisations.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because only parliaments/governments pass laws; pressure groups lobby lawmakers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: An animal welfare pressure group launches a viral social media video campaign exposing cramped cage conditions at a large egg producer, using a hashtag that trends nationally for two weeks. How does social media increase pressure group power?

options.A: It allows pressure groups to reach millions of consumers instantly at very low cost, threatening rapid brand damage
options.B: It legally forces supermarkets to close down within 24 hours
options.C: It prevents consumers from reading any news about the company
options.D: It eliminates the egg producer's feed and electricity expenses

correctAnswer: It allows pressure groups to reach millions of consumers instantly at very low cost, threatening rapid brand damage

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because viral digital campaigns amplify negative publicity at negligible cost, putting immediate reputational pressure on consumer brands.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because viral digital campaigns amplify negative publicity at negligible cost, putting immediate reputational pressure on consumer brands.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because social media generates reputational pressure, not automatic legal closure.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because viral posts *spread* information widely rather than hiding it.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because operating expenses are unaffected by social media hashtags.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: During a consumer boycott organised by an environmental pressure group against a bottled-water brand, what is the immediate financial risk to the targeted business?

options.A: Falling sales revenue and excess unsold inventory while fixed factory and marketing overheads continue
options.B: An immediate 50% increase in profit margins
options.C: A government subsidy compensating the firm for lost sales
options.D: Automatic elimination of all fixed overhead costs

correctAnswer: Falling sales revenue and excess unsold inventory while fixed factory and marketing overheads continue

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because boycotts reduce cash inflows from sales while fixed costs still have to be paid, squeezing profits and cash flow.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because boycotts reduce cash inflows from sales while fixed costs still have to be paid, squeezing profits and cash flow.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because lower sales volumes reduce rather than increase profits.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because governments do not compensate firms for consumer boycotts.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because rent, salaries, and loan interest remain payable.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A road-safety pressure group presents detailed crash statistics to transport ministers, persuading the government to make automatic emergency braking mandatory in all new cars. How has this pressure group affected car manufacturers?

options.A: Indirectly, by successfully lobbying the government to introduce new legal safety standards that manufacturers must obey
options.B: Directly, by buying 51% of shares in every car manufacturer
options.C: By banning all citizens from owning cars
options.D: By lowering car manufacturing costs to zero

correctAnswer: Indirectly, by successfully lobbying the government to introduce new legal safety standards that manufacturers must obey

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because pressure groups frequently influence business operations indirectly by convincing governments to legislate.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because pressure groups frequently influence business operations indirectly by convincing governments to legislate.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because the group used political lobbying, not a corporate takeover.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because cars remain legal with enhanced safety equipment.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adding mandatory safety sensors increases unit production costs.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why is a pressure group campaign against a well-known high-street fashion retailer much more likely to succeed than a campaign against an anonymous mining company that sells raw iron ore only to steel mills?

options.A: The fashion retailer relies directly on consumer brand image and faces thousands of retail competitors, whereas the mining firm has no direct retail shoppers to boycott it
options.B: Mining companies are legally immune from all environmental laws
options.C: Fashion retailers never care about sales revenue
options.D: Iron ore mining has zero impact on the environment

correctAnswer: The fashion retailer relies directly on consumer brand image and faces thousands of retail competitors, whereas the mining firm has no direct retail shoppers to boycott it

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because business-to-consumer (B2C) brands are highly sensitive to public reputation and consumer boycotts, unlike behind-the-scenes B2B commodity suppliers.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because business-to-consumer (B2C) brands are highly sensitive to public reputation and consumer boycotts, unlike behind-the-scenes B2B commodity suppliers.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because mining companies must obey environmental regulations.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because fashion retailers depend heavily on sales and brand appeal.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because mining has major environmental impacts, making it a target for lobbying rather than retail boycotts.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A disability rights pressure group audits the websites of 20 major online supermarkets and publishes a league table ranking them from most accessible to least accessible for blind and visually impaired shoppers. Why is publishing a league table effective?

options.A: Low-ranked supermarkets suffer public embarrassment and risk losing disabled shoppers and their families to higher-ranked rivals
options.B: League tables legally shut down the bottom ten supermarkets
options.C: Supermarkets prefer finishing at the bottom of public customer-service rankings
options.D: Blind shoppers never buy groceries online

correctAnswer: Low-ranked supermarkets suffer public embarrassment and risk losing disabled shoppers and their families to higher-ranked rivals

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because comparative public scorecards create peer competition and reputational pressure for laggards to improve.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because comparative public scorecards create peer competition and reputational pressure for laggards to improve.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because NGO league tables create reputational pressure, not legal closures.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because retailers strive to avoid negative public rankings.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because accessible online grocery shopping is hugely valuable for visually impaired customers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A local residents' pressure group opposes a delivery depot operating heavy lorries through narrow residential streets at 3:00 AM. How can the depot manager constructively resolve the conflict?

options.A: Meet with resident representatives, restrict heavy lorry movements to daytime hours, and reroute vehicles onto the main ring road
options.B: Increase 3:00 AM lorry deliveries through the residential streets
options.C: Refuse to speak to residents and ignore noise complaints
options.D: Close the entire business permanently without exploring route changes

correctAnswer: Meet with resident representatives, restrict heavy lorry movements to daytime hours, and reroute vehicles onto the main ring road

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because constructive stakeholder dialogue and practical operational adjustments resolve local friction without sacrificing the business.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because constructive stakeholder dialogue and practical operational adjustments resolve local friction without sacrificing the business.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because worsening the noise nuisance would provoke council enforcement and protests.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because ignoring valid community complaints risks local council night-time bans.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adjusting delivery times and routes solves the problem without closing the depot.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A pressure group calls for a boycott of the only pharmaceutical manufacturer producing a life-saving insulin medicine over high prices. Why will diabetic patients not participate in a consumer boycott?

options.A: Insulin is a vital life-saving necessity with no immediate substitute, so patients must keep buying it to survive
options.B: Diabetic patients do not care about medicine prices
options.C: Pharmaceutical companies give away all medicines for free
options.D: Pressure groups are legally banned from criticising drug prices

correctAnswer: Insulin is a vital life-saving necessity with no immediate substitute, so patients must keep buying it to survive

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because boycotts fail when the product is an essential necessity lacking close substitutes; pressure groups must instead lobby health regulators.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because boycotts fail when the product is an essential necessity lacking close substitutes; pressure groups must instead lobby health regulators.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because patients care deeply about high prices, which is why advocates lobby governments for price caps.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because commercial drugmakers charge prices to recover R&D and earn profits.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because advocacy groups regularly campaign on medicine affordability.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A coalition of 40 environmental and consumer pressure groups forms a joint campaign demanding a ban on toxic 'forever chemicals' (PFAS) in non-stick frying pans. Why is a coalition more effective than a single small pressure group?

options.A: Pooling funds, scientific researchers, media contacts, and millions of members creates far stronger political and commercial leverage
options.B: Coalitions are legally allowed to pass laws without Parliament
options.C: Coalitions eliminate all manufacturing costs for cookware firms
options.D: Single small pressure groups always have more money than 40 groups combined

correctAnswer: Pooling funds, scientific researchers, media contacts, and millions of members creates far stronger political and commercial leverage

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because uniting multiple organisations amplifies credibility, financial backing, and voter/consumer reach.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because uniting multiple organisations amplifies credibility, financial backing, and voter/consumer reach.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because coalitions still lobby lawmakers rather than passing laws themselves.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because switching away from PFAS requires R&D into alternative coatings.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because combining 40 organisations pools vastly greater resources.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: After pressure groups campaign against palm oil linked to rainforest deforestation, a biscuit manufacturer switches to 100% certified sustainable palm oil (RSPO) and partners with the conservation group to audit its plantations. What is a financial cost and a financial benefit of this decision?

options.A: Cost: higher raw ingredient prices and auditing fees; Benefit: protected brand reputation and continued sales to eco-conscious shoppers and supermarkets
options.B: Cost: lower ingredient prices; Benefit: loss of all supermarket contracts
options.C: Cost: zero expenses; Benefit: automatic exemption from corporation tax
options.D: Cost: closure of all biscuit factories; Benefit: lower labour productivity

correctAnswer: Cost: higher raw ingredient prices and auditing fees; Benefit: protected brand reputation and continued sales to eco-conscious shoppers and supermarkets

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because responding positively to pressure groups raises input/audit costs in the short term while safeguarding long-term sales and retail listings.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because responding positively to pressure groups raises input/audit costs in the short term while safeguarding long-term sales and retail listings.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because certified sustainable ingredients cost *more*, and supermarkets reward sustainable sourcing.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because certification carries real costs and does not waive corporation tax.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because the firm continues operating its factories.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A local heritage pressure group campaigns to stop a supermarket chain from demolishing a historic 19th-century Victorian train station to build a car park. The supermarket revises its plans to restore the historic station building as the entrance hall of its new store. Why was this compromise smart?

options.A: It won planning approval quickly, turned local critics into supporters, and created a distinctive, attractive store
options.B: It prevented the supermarket from opening any store in the town
options.C: It destroyed the historic building completely
options.D: It eliminated all construction expenses

correctAnswer: It won planning approval quickly, turned local critics into supporters, and created a distinctive, attractive store

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because adapting plans to address community concerns avoids costly legal planning delays and builds local goodwill.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because adapting plans to address community concerns avoids costly legal planning delays and builds local goodwill.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because the compromise enabled the store to open.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because the historic facade was restored rather than demolished.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because restoring a heritage building adds some upfront renovation expense.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why might a fast-food chain choose to reformulate its menu to lower salt and saturated fat levels after a health pressure group announces an upcoming national awareness campaign?

options.A: To pre-empt negative media coverage, avoid potential government taxes, and appeal to increasingly health-conscious families
options.B: Because salt and fat are illegal in all food products
options.C: Because pressure groups pay half of the restaurant's rent
options.D: To reduce customer visits by 50%

correctAnswer: To pre-empt negative media coverage, avoid potential government taxes, and appeal to increasingly health-conscious families

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because proactive adaptation neutralises bad publicity before it damages brand image and reduces the risk of statutory regulation.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because proactive adaptation neutralises bad publicity before it damages brand image and reduces the risk of statutory regulation.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because salt and fat are legal ingredients, though high levels attract health criticism.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because pressure groups do not subsidise business rent.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because healthier options help retain health-conscious customers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: When an oil company is targeted by climate protesters at major international sports events it sponsors, several sports governing bodies decide not to renew their sponsorship deals with the oil company. How has pressure group activity affected the oil company?

options.A: It has lost valuable brand-building sponsorship platforms due to reputational risk felt by its commercial partners
options.B: It has doubled its crude oil reserves automatically
options.C: It has been exempted from paying environmental taxes
options.D: It has gained free television advertising during all sports finals

correctAnswer: It has lost valuable brand-building sponsorship platforms due to reputational risk felt by its commercial partners

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because secondary pressure on business partners (such as sports bodies, banks, or insurers) isolates targeted firms from mainstream marketing channels.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because secondary pressure on business partners (such as sports bodies, banks, or insurers) isolates targeted firms from mainstream marketing channels.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because losing sports sponsorships does not create oil reserves.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because sponsorship losses do not reduce taxes.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because losing sponsorship removes brand visibility at major events.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A small fringe group with no scientific evidence claims on a blog that 5G mobile phone masts cause illness and demands that telecom companies dismantle all masts. Why will telecom companies ignore the demand to remove masts while publishing clear scientific safety facts?

options.A: Dismantling masts would destroy an essential modern service, while the group lacks scientific credibility or broad public backing; calm factual PR reassures customers
options.B: Telecom companies are legally required to dismantle masts whenever one person complains
options.C: 5G networks operate without any masts or antennas
options.D: Scientific facts are banned from company websites

correctAnswer: Dismantling masts would destroy an essential modern service, while the group lacks scientific credibility or broad public backing; calm factual PR reassures customers

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because businesses distinguish between credible, widely supported pressure groups and unfounded fringe claims, responding to the latter with factual communication.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because businesses distinguish between credible, widely supported pressure groups and unfounded fringe claims, responding to the latter with factual communication.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because unfounded complaints do not trigger legal shutdowns.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because mobile networks physically require base-station masts.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because companies routinely publish independent health and safety data.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A passenger-rights pressure group lobbies the government to force airlines to pay automatic cash compensation of $400 whenever a flight is delayed by more than three hours due to airline fault. How does this affect airlines' operations?

options.A: It increases potential penalty costs for delays, motivating airlines to invest in better aircraft maintenance and realistic flight schedules
options.B: It allows airlines to delay flights indefinitely without informing passengers
options.C: It eliminates aviation fuel taxes for delayed flights
options.D: It forces passengers to pay airlines $400 when a flight is delayed

correctAnswer: It increases potential penalty costs for delays, motivating airlines to invest in better aircraft maintenance and realistic flight schedules

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because consumer-protection laws achieved by pressure groups create financial penalties that push firms to improve reliability.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because consumer-protection laws achieved by pressure groups create financial penalties that push firms to improve reliability.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because mandatory compensation penalises, rather than encourages, avoidable delays.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because passenger compensation rules do not waive fuel taxes.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because the airline compensates the delayed passenger.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: An anti-gambling pressure group persuades television broadcasters and football clubs to stop accepting shirt sponsorships from online betting companies. What is the direct business impact on online betting firms?

options.A: Loss of major mass-market advertising channels, making customer acquisition harder and potentially slowing revenue growth
options.B: Lower corporation tax rates on gambling profits
options.C: Automatic doubling of active online gamblers
options.D: Elimination of all website server costs

correctAnswer: Loss of major mass-market advertising channels, making customer acquisition harder and potentially slowing revenue growth

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because restricting high-visibility sponsorship channels limits a firm's promotional mix and brand exposure.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because restricting high-visibility sponsorship channels limits a firm's promotional mix and brand exposure.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because advertising restrictions do not lower tax rates.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because losing major sports visibility tends to slow customer sign-ups.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because IT and server overheads remain unchanged.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: How can a business's employees themselves act similarly to an internal pressure group on ethical and environmental issues?

options.A: Skilled employees may sign open letters, threaten to resign, or refuse to work on projects they view as unethical or environmentally destructive

options.C: Employees can set the central bank's base interest rate
options.D: Employees never care about the ethical reputation of their employer

correctAnswer: Skilled employees may sign open letters, threaten to resign, or refuse to work on projects they view as unethical or environmentally destructive

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because modern employees—especially scarce tech and professional staff—frequently push management to drop unethical contracts or adopt green targets.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because modern employees—especially scarce tech and professional staff—frequently push management to drop unethical contracts or adopt green targets.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because only elected legislatures pass national laws.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because central banks set monetary policy.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because workplace values strongly influence employee morale and retention.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A consumer pressure group publishes test results showing that a popular brand of children's car seats fails high-speed side-impact safety tests, even though it passed older minimum legal tests. Why will the manufacturer recall and redesign the seat immediately?

options.C: Because redesigning car seats costs zero money
options.D: Because parents prefer cheaper car seats even if they fail crash tests

correctAnswer: Because no parent will buy a car seat perceived as unsafe, so ignoring the report would permanently destroy the brand

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because for safety-critical family products, credible independent safety criticism collapses demand overnight unless resolved immediately.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because for safety-critical family products, credible independent safety criticism collapses demand overnight unless resolved immediately.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because consumer groups publish test results rather than exercising police arrest powers.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because product recalls and engineering redesigns are very costly, yet essential for survival.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because safety is the primary purchasing criterion for child car seats.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A farming trade association (a business pressure group) lobbies the government to block imports of cheap foreign beef produced with growth hormones banned domestically. What is the trade association trying to achieve?

options.A: Protect domestic farmers from lower-cost foreign competition by insisting imports meet the same strict production standards
options.B: Lower domestic beef prices by 50% to hurt local farmers
options.C: Ban domestic consumers from ever eating beef
options.D: Increase corporation taxes on domestic farms

correctAnswer: Protect domestic farmers from lower-cost foreign competition by insisting imports meet the same strict production standards

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because producer pressure groups lobby governments for trade rules and standards that protect their members' livelihoods and competitiveness.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why do pressure groups often time their protests, reports, and boycotts to coincide with major corporate events such as a new product launch or the holiday shopping season?

options.C: Businesses close all their shops during the holiday shopping season
options.D: Consumers stop reading news during product launches

distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because peaceful protests are legal year-round.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because peak shopping seasons are when stores are busiest and most vulnerable to disruption.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A toy retailer stops selling plastic water pistols and war-themed toys after parents' pressure groups campaign against violent toys for young children. How does this decision affect the retailer?

options.A: It loses sales from that specific product line, but strengthens its family-friendly brand image and wins approval from parents
options.B: It is forced to close all its toy shops permanently
options.C: It receives a government fine for changing its product range
options.D: All other educational toys become impossible to sell

correctAnswer: It loses sales from that specific product line, but strengthens its family-friendly brand image and wins approval from parents

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: When evaluating the impact of a pressure group's boycott on a multinational business, why is it important to consider whether the boycott is local or international?

options.A: A boycott limited to one small town barely affects a global MNC's total revenue, whereas a coordinated international boycott across major markets threatens global profits
options.B: A local boycott in one town always bankrupts a multinational corporation
options.C: International boycotts have zero effect on multinational companies
options.D: Multinational companies only sell products in one small town

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because scale matters: an MNC's geographic diversification insulates it from isolated local protests unless the campaign spreads internationally.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because one small town represents a tiny fraction of a global MNC's sales.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because global boycotts across key markets can severely hit MNC revenues and share prices.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because MNCs operate across multiple countries.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A pressure group campaigns against a major bank's plans to close its last remaining rural bank branches, arguing that elderly residents and small rural shops will be unable to deposit cash. How could the bank respond to satisfy both cost-cutting goals and the pressure group?

options.A: Share banking hubs with other banks in rural post offices or run mobile banking vans on scheduled days rather than leaving villages with zero service
options.B: Close all branches immediately without offering any alternative services
options.C: Keep every large, loss-making branch open 24 hours a day seven days a week
options.D: Charge rural elderly customers $50 every time they check their balance

correctAnswer: Share banking hubs with other banks in rural post offices or run mobile banking vans on scheduled days rather than leaving villages with zero service

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because shared banking hubs and mobile vans cut fixed branch overheads while preserving essential community access and goodwill.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because shared banking hubs and mobile vans cut fixed branch overheads while preserving essential community access and goodwill.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because total abandonment fuels fierce public and political backlash.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because keeping underused branches open 24/7 is financially unsustainable.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because punitive fees would outrage regulators and customers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: How do pressure groups act as an 'early warning system' for forward-thinking business managers?

options.A: They highlight emerging social, ethical, and environmental concerns early, giving proactive firms time to adapt before laws change or scandals erupt
options.B: They secretly manage the business's daily payroll and accounting
options.C: They guarantee that consumer tastes will never change
options.D: They prevent governments from ever passing new regulations

correctAnswer: They highlight emerging social, ethical, and environmental concerns early, giving proactive firms time to adapt before laws change or scandals erupt

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because pressure group campaigns often signal future shifts in consumer expectations and legislation, enabling early movers to gain a competitive edge.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because pressure group campaigns often signal future shifts in consumer expectations and legislation, enabling early movers to gain a competitive edge.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because pressure groups are external bodies, not internal administrators.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because pressure groups actively drive changes in consumer attitudes.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because pressure groups frequently campaign *for* new regulations.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A multinational food manufacturer faces sustained pressure group campaigns over plastic packaging, high sugar content, and supply-chain deforestation. Which comprehensive strategic response is most effective for long-term business survival?

options.A: Set measurable, independently verified targets for recyclable packaging, healthier product reformulation, and deforestation-free sourcing, and report progress transparently
options.B: Spend millions on misleading green adverts without changing any ingredients or packaging
options.C: Ignore all pressure groups, consumers, and lawmakers until sales collapse
options.D: Close the company and return all assets to the government

correctAnswer: Set measurable, independently verified targets for recyclable packaging, healthier product reformulation, and deforestation-free sourcing, and report progress transparently

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because genuine operational reform backed by transparent verification addresses the root causes of external pressure and secures long-term competitiveness.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because genuine operational reform backed by transparent verification addresses the root causes of external pressure and secures long-term competitiveness.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because greenwashing backfires severely when exposed by pressure groups and regulators.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because ignoring major external shifts in consumer and regulatory expectations leads to long-term decline.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adapting products and supply chains allows the business to thrive profitably.
